name: CAMELYON16: Cancer Metastases in Lymph Nodes Challenge 2016
description: CAMELYON16 is a landmark digital pathology benchmark for automated detection of metastases in whole-slide histopathology images (WSIs) of breast cancer sentinel lymph node sections. Organized by Radboud University Medical Center and University Medical Center Utrecht in conjunction with ISBI 2016, the dataset contains 400 gigapixel WSIs (270 training slides including 110 with nodal metastases and 160 normal slides, plus 130 test slides). Metastatic regions are delineated with detailed pixel-level ground-truth annotations by expert pathologists, establishing the gold standard for clinical-grade lymph node metastasis detection and whole-slide evaluation algorithms.

publisher.name: Radboud University Medical Center & UMC Utrecht

license.name: Conflicting: CC0 1.0 (Data Portal & GigaDB) vs CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Download) vs Challenge Rules
license.notes: Conflicting authoritative terms exist across project documentation: The CAMELYON17 /Data/ portal, GigaScience Database (DOI: 10.5524/100439), and AWS Open Data Registry state CC0 1.0 Universal; conversely, the CAMELYON17 /Download/ page displays a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license badge, and CAMELYON16 Challenge Rules forbid redistribution and commercial algorithm development without prior challenge participation. Commercial permissions are unresolved and marked as unknown.

provenance.collection_method: Whole-slide digital scanning of hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained sentinel lymph node tissue sections.
provenance.curation_notes: The challenge dataset officially distributed 400 whole-slide images (270 training: 160 normal, 110 metastasis; 130 testing: 80 normal, 50 metastasis). In the landmark evaluation published in JAMA 2017 (Bejnordi et al., DOI: 10.1001/jama.2017.14585), 399 slides were evaluated (270 training, 129 testing), with one test slide excluded from the evaluation.
